summary: Manakara Airport (WVK) is a regional domestic airport serving the coastal town of Manakara on Madagascar's southeastern coast, along the Indian Ocean. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting the Fitovinany region with Antananarivo and other Malagasy cities, mainly operated by Tsaradia. The airport is a gateway to one of Madagascar's key vanilla-producing areas and offers access to the historic Manakara–Fianarantsoa railway, one of the few functioning rail lines in the country.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Manakara Airport?
A: Domestic flights are primarily operated by Tsaradia, the regional subsidiary of Air Madagascar, with regular service to Antananarivo.

Q: How far is Manakara Airport from the town center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers south of central Manakara, typically a short taxi or tuk-tuk ride away.

Q: Is Manakara Airport international?
A: No, WVK is a domestic-only facility handling regional flights within Madagascar.

Q: What is the best time to fly into Manakara?
A: The dry season from May to October generally offers the most reliable weather and smoother flight operations.
transport_tips: Taxis and tuk-tuks are the main options for getting to and from Manakara Airport, and they are usually available upon arrival. Roads connecting the airport to town are paved but can be in poor condition, so allow extra travel time during the rainy season. Many travelers combine a flight with the historic Manakara–Fianarantsoa railway journey to reach inland destinations.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time, visit the nearby Manakara market to sample fresh vanilla, cloves, and local seafood—some of the freshest vanilla in Madagascar comes directly from surrounding farms.
